paper: Scorecard of AI Evaluation Quality (San Joaquin, Gipiskis, Chin — Feb 2026)
assessed_by: CRO (Cetalabs) — SELF-assessment, 2026-11-20. We authored this suite, so this is the weakest form of grading and has no standing against a third-party assessment of the same work.
evidence_read: suites/sme-whatsapp/persona.json — the case context supplied to the agent (authored)
suites/sme-whatsapp/items.json — 20 scenarios, each with pre-written expected behaviour and a policy_field anchor (authored)
suites/sme-whatsapp/sme_eval.py — the three scorers, the lazy grader, the solver/grader independence assert (authored, then debugged against real failures)
Measured gate: oracle safety 0.900 / helpfulness 1.000; naive safety 0.000 / helpfulness 0.315; critical-failure flags oracle 0/20, naive 20/20
Mechanical check: all 20 items' policy_fields resolve against persona.json — 0 dangling references
scoring_note: Each dimension scored 1 (best) to 4 (worst). Classification from Table 7: the HIGHEST category whose minimum component per dimension is met. The paper's colour-downgrade rule (§3.1) is NOT applied — highlight colours do not survive markdown extraction and inventing them would fabricate the grade. Scores are assigned from the §3.2–3.6 item lists.

headline_for_the_requester.requested: Make the dataset Grade C or Grade B.
headline_for_the_requester.actually_graded: D. And it cannot honestly be graded C yet, for one specific reason.
headline_for_the_requester.why: Table 7 requires External Validity <= 1 for BOTH B and C. External Validity 1 requires that the design be informed by the people the system affects. This suite was authored entirely by the evaluating party. No car-rental operator has reviewed the 20 scenarios, the persona, the expected verdicts, or the harm severities. That requirement is not a formality and I will not assert it.
headline_for_the_requester.what_this_means: The suite is BUILT to the C standard — every other dimension is at 2, which satisfies C and nearly satisfies B. Only the external review is missing. One documented review session with an SME operator moves this to C, and SME_REVIEW_SHEET.md in this directory exists to make that a checkable step rather than a promise.

sme_whatsapp_reply_agent.display: SME WhatsApp Reply Agent — Malaysian car rental v1.0
sme_whatsapp_reply_agent.status: v1.0. Grade D, capped solely by External Validity. Built to the C standard; C is one documented SME review away.

satisfied: THREE sub-components scored separately and deliberately, named per the score-v1 rubric: safety (no unauthorised or invented business commitment), helpfulness (advances the customer's legitimate objective), customer support (register, proportional empathy, language fit). A single 'good reply' number could not separate 'polite but promised a refund the owner never authorised' from 'correct but reads like a bank chatbot'.
Per-item operational definition written BEFORE any model ran: expected_reply, the policy field that makes it correct (grounding_anchor), and harm_if_failed with a severity.
Balance across three inquiry types — 7 normal, 8 problems, 5 feedback — plus 8 high-harm, 10 medium, 2 low. A happy-path-only suite cannot be mistaken for coverage.
Escalation is a SCORED outcome rather than a failure: 10 items require referring the decision to the owner, so 'the agent invents policy' cannot score well.

Anti-collapse controls in the other direction: 2 items (W13 breakdown, W16 praise) are deliberately NOT escalation cases, so 'escalate everything' cannot score well either. This is the control condition.
Within-fleet exception included (Hilux: manual, CDW unavailable, highest excess) — a reply can get this wrong without any other item noticing.
The case is a fully specified policy document, so every item is answerable from context and none depends on outside knowledge.
gaps: n=20 is small. No sampling justification, no statistical power, no claim that 20 scenarios represent the SME WhatsApp task space.

The sub-component boundaries were drawn by one author with no second opinion on whether 'customer support' and 'helpfulness' are genuinely separable in practice — they correlate by construction on some items.
Only one business type is covered. Nothing here transfers to a clinic, a tuition centre or a restaurant, though the enquiry types do.
No pure-BM items. 5 Manglish, 15 English. For a Malaysian suite this is a substantive scope failure and it means results do not transfer to a BM-language deployment.
construct_validity.justification: Three separated sub-components, pre-specified pass rules, a declared escalation rule, and controls pushing in BOTH directions (invent-nothing vs escalate-nothing) is strong design and materially better than the single-score suites in this repo. Not a 1 because n=20 is unjustified and English-only limits the construct.

satisfied: TWO of the three scores are computed by deterministic code with no model anywhere in the loop, so they carry no grader-identity effect at all — a stronger guarantee than picking an independent grader model.

The third (customer support) is model-graded by a model asserted OUTSIDE the five-solver set, and run_matrix.sh independently re-checks that the grader is not in the solver list before starting. The independence requirement is enforced twice.
A pre-run selftest proves the safety and helpfulness markers, and the measured result separates cleanly: oracle safety 0.900 / helpfulness 1.000 against naive safety 0.000 / helpfulness 0.315.

The fabrication detector is validated in the strong direction: it raised the critical-failure flag on 20 of 20 naive replies AND on 0 of 20 oracle replies. Catching every fabrication while never firing on a correct answer is precisely the property that was missing in the sibling suites, where markers repeatedly fired on correct answers.

Promises and invented terms are matched with a negation guard, so a correct reply that says 'we do NOT waive that' cannot be read as promising a waiver. This bug class produced false results eight times elsewhere in this repo; here it is guarded from the outset.
The critical-failure override is implemented per score-v1 §2 rather than folded into the continuous scale.
gaps: customer_support is model-graded, so one of the three scores is a property of two models. A grader swap would move it. The suite declares the grader explicitly rather than leaving it implicit, but the sensitivity is real and unmeasured.

No human-agreement study. The paper's central internal-validity requirement is that automated scoring be validated against human judgement on the SAME items. The selftest validates against author-written oracle text, which is weaker: it proves the marker matches its author, not that it matches a competent reviewer.

A recorded near-miss counts against this dimension: the first full matrix run produced 20/20 empty completions and status=error on ALL FIVE models, caused by passing raw JSON to system_message() (its template engine reads every brace as a substitution). It was caught by reading the logs rather than the console, but it is direct evidence that the harness — not the model — is the dominant failure source on a new suite.
The selftest does not cover customer_support at all (it is proven by the mock task pair instead), so no single command validates all three scorers.
internal_validity.justification: Deterministic marking for two of three scores, double-enforced grader independence, and a fabrication detector validated in both directions (20/20 caught, 0/20 false) is genuinely strong and is the reason this is a 2. Not a 1 because there is no human-agreement study on the actual items, and the harness produced a total failure on the first attempt.

satisfied: The scenario mix is grounded in documented recurring themes of Malaysian SME customer service rather than invented: deposit-refund chasing, unexpected insurance excess, handover-staff complaints, peak-date pricing surprises, late-return waiver requests, and discount asks buried in positive feedback.

The persona is a CONSTRUCTED COMPOSITE with a fully specified policy document, so every item is answerable from the case and none depends on knowing a real business. This is a deliberate methodological choice, not an accident.
The suite declares what it does not cover, in the items file and the registry caveat, rather than leaving the gaps to be discovered.
SME_REVIEW_SHEET.md ships alongside, turning the missing requirement into a concrete, checkable artefact.
gaps: NO USER OR DOMAIN-EXPERT REVIEW HAS TAKEN PLACE. The paper's primary external-validity requirement is that design be informed by the people affected. Every scenario, verdict, harm severity and register judgement reflects one author's model of how a Malaysian rental operator writes and decides. Zero car-rental operators, zero SME owners, zero consumer representatives have seen it.

The persona's policy figures (rates, deposit, excess, surcharges) are plausible and internally consistent but are not taken from any real business's published terms. A real operator might find the whole term structure unfamiliar.

The harm severities are author-assigned with no operator input on which failures would actually cost the business most. W11 (deposit delay) is scored high volume-harm partly on my reasoning, not an operator's.
English and Manglish only; no BM. A BM-language deployment is not represented.

The register targets ('warm but not groveling', 'casual Manglish') are an outsider's model of Malaysian SME WhatsApp tone, which is exactly the kind of judgement a domain expert would most likely correct.
external_validity.justification: The inquiry mix is grounded in documented real patterns and the case is fully specified, which is more than most hand-authored suites manage. But no affected user has reviewed it, and the paper makes that the first requirement of this dimension. A 2 is the honest score; a 1 would be a claim I cannot support. THIS IS THE CAPPING DIMENSION and the only thing standing between this suite and Category C.

satisfied: Deterministic for safety and helpfulness — identical input yields identical output, with no sampling or model involvement.
The item set and persona are version-controlled, so every change to a verdict or a policy figure is visible in the diff.
Stored Eval Logs can be re-scored offline at zero API cost after any marker change, which is how the sibling suites' erroneous first numbers were corrected.
The five-solver matrix reads its model list from the eval module, so the shell script cannot silently diverge from what the eval actually scores.
Empty completions are detected and excluded rather than read as failures — the failure mode that produced a false 'catastrophic' result in a sibling suite.
gaps: customer_support depends on a grader model that will drift as the provider updates it; the same replies may score differently in six months with no change to the suite. Nothing monitors this.
No inter-rater or test-retest study, and no repeated run to check score stability across identical conditions.
The maker/checker is one person, and the marker's own author wrote the oracle text it is validated against.
reliability.justification: Deterministic core scoring, version control, free offline re-scoring and empty-completion handling make this reproducible run-to-run. Not a 1 because one of three scores rides on an externally-drifting grader and no stability study exists.

satisfied: Every item's answer key is MECHANICALLY TRACEABLE to the case document: each declares policy_fields, and all 20 resolve against persona.json with zero dangling references. This was verified by script, not by memory, and it is checked for the whole set at once.

Because the persona IS the ground truth, there is no external fact in the answer key at all — no statute, no market price from a named competitor, no regulator reference. The unverified-statutory-placeholder problem that burdens a sibling suite is absent by construction.
The case document is supplied to the agent verbatim, so the evaluated model and the answer key read the same source. Disagreement is therefore about reasoning, not about missing information.

The policy contains deliberate internal exceptions (weekly = 6 days' price, +40% peak, CDW unavailable on the Hilux, two separate foreign-customer rules) so the key cannot be satisfied by a model guessing a plausible default.
gaps: SINGLE-AUTHORED GROUND TRUTH. Every expected verdict is one person's judgement of correct small-business practice. No second rater, no operator sign-off, no inter-rater agreement figure.

The expected replies are plausible rather than authoritative: a real operator might legitimately handle several items differently — for example, choosing to escalate W13 (breakdown) for insurance reasons, which the key treats as a non-escalation item.

The scoring bands are mapped from the score-v1 rubric by one author; the mapping from 'warm but not groveling' to a 0.8-versus-1.0 distinction is a judgement that has never been calibrated against a second reader.

The grader model's own output has not been audited against the anchors on the actual replies — the model-graded dimension could be systematically generous or harsh and nothing would currently reveal it.
correctness.justification: A fully traceable, internally consistent, externally-fact-free answer key of 20 items is a real strength and better than the sibling suites, where answer-key defects needed external research to establish. Not a 1 because the key remains one author's opinion with no independent check, and the model-graded dimension's calibration is unaudited.
